verdict.outcome_rationale: This was a genuine agent-fault partial failure—the verifier's FAIL is correct. The hidden harness found /app/solution.py and awarded binary_reward 0 with fractional score 0.667 after Steps 76.1 and 76.2 passed but Step 76.4 failed on an assertion that scan_sequence(sequence, load_motif_from_df(data), 0.8) must match a precomputed target [1][2]. The task required four integrated functions in /app/solution.py, including generate_dna that builds a uniform-length background, its reverse complement, and a PWM-sampled insertion at a random position p with 0 ≤ p < N, then scan_sequence that thresholds log-odds at scale·KLD and returns the most frequent hit over num_runs [3][4]. The agent implemented load_motif_from_df and compute_kld correctly (matching reference L2-normalize-after-+1 and Σ p·log(p/0.25)) [2][5], but its generate_dna first samples the N-length uniform background and PWM motif, only then draws p, and builds new_seq_rc by reverse-complementing the already-extended new_seq rather than reverse-complementing the N-length uniform background and inserting the spike at N−p [6][7]. Because Step 76.4 tests seed random to 42, call the agent's own generate_dna, and assert scan_sequence on that sequence against reference targets, this ordering and RC construction produce a different insertion index and sequence (e.g., p=148 vs the reference p=163 for the first test case) even though the agent's scan_sequence logic matches the reference when given the same input sequence [4][6][7]. The agent ran only ad-hoc self-tests on its own pipeline—reporting 13/20 and 109/200 recovery rates—and concluded the solution was correct without exercising the seeded generate_dna contract that the verifier indirectly enforces [8][9]. Steps 1–2 are sound, but the task as a whole is not solved, so TN is appropriate and the verifier is not at fault.

evidence.claim: The instruction requires generate_dna to produce a uniform N-length background, its reverse complement, and a PWM-sampled insertion at a random position p with 0 ≤ p < N, plus scan_sequence that records windows exceeding scale·KLD and returns the most frequent position.

citations.quote: Given length and PWM, write a sequence generator that generates DNA sequence of the length with uniform distribution and its reverse complement with insertion of sequence that was sampled from the PWM. For the insertion location, it should be a random non-negative integer < length.

If the logodds exceeds `scale * compute_kld(matrix)`, record the window start position. Run the scanner many times and return the most frequent output position. If no position is detected, return `None`.

evidence.claim: The reference generate_dna draws insertion position p first, builds an N-length uniform background, reverse-complements that background, then splices the PWM-sampled spike into new_seq at p and into new_seq_rc at N−p.

citations.quote:
p = random.randint(0, N-1)
    dna_string = ''.join(random.choices(nucleotide, uni_weights, k=N))
    ...
    reverse_complement = ''.join(complement[nuc] for nuc in reversed_seq if nuc in complement)
    new_seq = dna_string[:p] + spiked_seq + dna_string[p:]
    new_seq_rc = reverse_complement[:N-p] + spiked_seq + reverse_complement[N-p:]

evidence.claim: The agent's load_motif_from_df adds 1 to each PWM entry and L2-normalizes each row, and compute_kld sums matrix·log(matrix/0.25), matching the Step 1–2 specification.

    norms = np.linalg.norm(mat, axis=1, keepdims=True)

evidence.claim: The agent's generate_dna samples the uniform background and PWM motif before drawing p, splices the motif into new_seq, and reverse-complements the extended new_seq rather than the N-length background.

citations.quote:
seq = [random.choice(BASES) for _ in range(N)]
    ...
    p = random.randint(0, N - 1)
    new_seq = ''.join(seq[:p] + motif + seq[p:])
    new_seq_rc = ''.join(COMPLEMENT[b] for b in reversed(new_seq))

evidence.claim: The agent's scan_sequence slides a motif-length window, sums log(matrix[j,base]/0.25), thresholds at scale·compute_kld(matrix), repeats num_runs times, and returns Counter.most_common—structurally equivalent to the reference scanner.
The agent validated only its own end-to-end pipeline with a custom PWM and reported partial recovery rates (13/20 exact hits, 109 ok / 75 none / 16 wrong over 200 trials).
